geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the flat bar into a hall macro so section can be authored as a gymnasium rather than a generic extrusion.
A ridge section best supports clear-span hall logic and daylight expression for the gym program.
Wrap the hall with a small courtyard threshold so the verified access edge becomes legible as public ground.
Use a modest margin to carve a clear but compact entry court without erasing the hall mass.
Align the opening to the program-frame access side so the mass responds to arrival.
Make the court the new root so the hall remains in ancestry while the frontage logic becomes primary.

graph_edits.rationale: Introduce a section-readable roof family so the hall can express span/daylight instead of remaining a flat bar.
Ridge is the most compatible balanced slot for a compact gym hall and directly supports span logic.
Add a public void at the access edge so the frontage reads as a threshold rather than a sealed bar.
Keep the void bounded and proportionate to the compact hall while making it legible in plan and elevation.
Open the court toward the site access side in the program frame to align the public threshold with arrival.

rationale: The candidate is a simple rectilinear bar that reads cleanly in all four views and stays within the parcel, so repair integrity is high. However, for a gymnasium it is too generic and under-articulated: there is no legible long-span hall section, no roof/daylight logic, and almost no public void or entry threshold on the verified access edge. The mass is coherent but semantically flat, closer to a basic bar building than a compact training hall. The blue frontage is not answered by a meaningful court, undercut, or seam, so the access response is weak. It can be salvaged as a protected anchor, but the next iteration needs a carved public threshold and a section gesture that expresses span rather than a plain box.
